claims.text: Irradiation introduces point defects into bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
Point defects scatter phonons in bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
Phonon scattering by irradiation-induced point defects reduces the lattice contribution to thermal conductivity relative to unchanged bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
The predicted reduction applies from 0 to 200 K in bulk HfNbTaTiZr containing irradiation-induced point defects.
There are no direct experimental data establishing the effect of point defects on thermal conductivity in HfNbTaTiZr.
Combined thermal-conductivity and electrical-resistivity measurements can separate lattice and electronic heat-transport contributions.
Failure to observe a lower inferred lattice thermal conductivity in irradiated material than in an unirradiated control over the specified temperature range would falsify the hypothesis.
